issue: QC's worklist proposed Capacity 7.74 -> 7.30 bcm/y (Natalia's 7.74 was deliberately switched to the MAXIMUM design rating on 2026-07-24, per her own ResearcherNotesUnit: 'Updated capacity to maximum capacity as per the most recent source'; QC's suggested 7.30 assumes the methodology wants NOMINAL, derived from the sponsor's 20 Mm3/day figure). I independently pulled the underlying source (energymag.gr/116159) and it explicitly separates the two ratings: 6,378 MWh/h (nominal) vs 9,567 MWh/h (maximum) -- the SAME article cited for the live 7.74 value. Converting the nominal 6,378 MWh/h proportionally against the live 7.74-from-9,567 basis gives ~5.16-5.17 bcm/y for nominal, NOT the 7.30 figure QC's worklist cites -- I could not independently reproduce 7.30 from any source I read (LNG Prime's '20 Mm3/day' framing is ambiguous as to nominal-vs-max and I could not confirm it corresponds to 7.30 bcm/y on GEM's own unit basis). I am NOT staging a Capacity edit in either direction (neither the worklist's 7.30 nor my own computed ~5.17): unlike liquefaction trains (nameplate vs peak is well-defined per unit_conventions.md), regasification/FSRU import capacity may be industry-conventionally quoted as MAXIMUM design send-out rate rather than nominal -- I have no confirmation of which convention GEM's own Capacity field intends for FSRU/regas terminals specifically, so overriding Natalia's deliberate, sourced 7.74-as-maximum entry risks being just as wrong as her switch may have been. This also trips the Update SOP's >20% capacity-swing pause-and-ask trigger (7.74 -> 5.17 or 7.30 is a 33% / 6% swing depending which comparison, and 7.74 vs the worklist's 7.30 alone is a 6% swing, but 7.74 vs my computed nominal ~5.17 is 33%).
suggested_action: Reviewer must resolve the underlying question -- does GEM's Capacity field for FSRU/regas terminals intend nominal (contract/guaranteed) send-out or maximum (design peak) send-out -- before any edit is made, ideally by checking the methodology doc's regasification-capacity convention section and/or how other GEM FSRU rows (e.g. Alexandroupolis, which lists 5.50 bcm/y alongside a noted TYNDP figure of 8.3) were resolved. Until that convention is settled, leave Thessaloniki Capacity at the live value (7.74, sourced, deliberate) rather than reverting to an unreproduced 7.30 or overriding with an independently-computed 5.17 nominal figure.
